paragraphs.source_en: A devoted son, Hideyoshi had departed Nagoya for the capital as soon as word reached him that the Ōmandokoro was gravely ill; only upon arriving in Osaka on the twenty-ninth did he learn that his mother had already died. Because he had been absorbed in the war, the truth had been kept from him, and he had lost his chance to see his aged mother one last time.

paragraphs.source_en: The Korean campaign may broadly be divided into four phases: the landing and advance on the capital, the commanders’ pacification of the eight provinces, the fighting between Japan and Ming China, and the withdrawal and negotiations.

paragraphs.source_en: During this time the court had tried to prevent Hideyoshi from crossing the sea, and the Ōmandokoro had fallen ill as well... For Hideyoshi, these truly were one ill omen after another. paragraphs.source_en: From this time onward, Hideyoshi must privately have been considering peace with Korea and Ming China. Peace negotiations could not be conducted at Jurakudai, which he had already promised to Hidetsugu; he needed a place where the other side’s envoys could be received, and this was why he intended to build a castle at Fushimi. paragraphs.source_en: From the daimyō who had not joined the Korean expedition, Hideyoshi levied twenty-four laborers for every ten thousand koku of income, raising thirty-five thousand men in all, and began constructing Fushimi Castle.
